claims.text: Nanoparticle structural and chemical stability is governed by preservation of the initial solid-solution phase.
Suppression of elemental segregation or phase separation governs nanoparticle stability.
The proposed stability relationship holds from 473 to 1923 K under an inert atmosphere at pressures below 1 atm.
The proposed stability relationship holds when the temperature ramp rate does not exceed 10 K/min and dwell time at each step is at least 30 minutes.
Uniform elemental distribution within the solid solution facilitates suppression of elemental segregation or phase separation.
A lack of significant crystal-structure changes facilitates suppression of elemental segregation or phase separation.
Interactions between the constituent metals influence segregation and phase-separation behavior.
Relative atomic ratios of the constituent metals influence segregation and phase-separation behavior.
Under the specified conditions, the lattice parameter will deviate by less than 5% from its initial value.
Under the specified conditions, chemical composition will deviate by less than 5% from its initial value.
The defined test uses a ramp rate of 5 K/min and a dwell time of 60 minutes at each temperature step.
The exact role of each constituent metal in suppressing segregation or phase separation is not fully understood.
Impurity and defect effects are not included in the hypothesis.
A deviation greater than 15% in lattice parameter or chemical composition at any tested temperature is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
A deviation below 10% in the nominally unstable control is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires less than 5% deviation, but the hypothesis is only falsified above 15%, leaving outcomes from 5% through 15% that violate the stated prediction without meeting the falsification rule.
